## Circular to SFC's Registered Intermediaries

## Guidelines for Exemptions from the Recognised Industry Qualification and Local Regulatory Framework Paper Requirements

In April 2001, the Commission introduced the competence requirements with the objective of ensuring that licensed persons are adequately equipped to carry out their functions and are aware of their legal responsibilities.  Applicants seeking to be licensed by the Commission may demonstrate competence by obtaining certain recognised industry qualification and by passing a local regulatory framework examination.

With  a  view  to  facilitating entry to the securities  and  futures  industry  but  without compromising  investor  protection,  the  Commission  may  consider  granting  an  exemption from  the  recognised  industry  qualification  if  the  applicant  has  attained  certain  level  of academic achievement or possesses sufficient relevant working experience.

For applicant seeking exemption from the applicable local regulatory framework paper(s), the Commission may take into consideration the following factors:

- (a) experience of the applicant;
- (b) scope of activities the applicant will engage in;
- (c) regulatory support from other personnel; and
- (d) internal control system of the corporation to which the applicant will accredit.

Representatives seeking licence for another regulated activity under a different Ordinance may also apply for exemption from taking the regulatory framework paper.

However, all individual applicants seeking exemption from the regulatory framework paper have to fulfill, among other things, additional five Continuous Professional Training hours in the specific area.

While  it  is  at  the  sole  discretion  of  the  Commission  in  granting  any  exemption,  extra regulatory  comfort  such  as  conditions  on  the  licensed  corporation  and/or  the  individual applicant and undertakings by the licensed corporation, may be required.

For  details,  please  refer  to  the  attached Guidelines  for  Exemptions  from  the  Recognised Industry Qualification and Local Regulatory Framework Paper Requirements.

If you have any enquiries regarding the above, please refer to the sub-section of "Frequently Asked  Questions  on  Competence"  under  the  'Intermediaries,  Licensing  and  Investment Products - Licensing Related Matters' section of the SFC website at www.hksfc.org.hk, or contact your responsible Intermediaries Relationship Manager of the Licensing Department.
